nodes.title: The exceptional primes of E
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve of conductor N and j-invariant j_E. Its exceptional set Σ_E is the finite set of primes p such that p ≤ 5, or p ∣ N, or p ∣ v_ℓ(j_E) for some prime ℓ with v_ℓ(N) = 1, or E admits a ℚ-rational cyclic subgroup of order p. Every p ∉ Σ_E is good for E and E[p] is irreducible.
hypotheses: Σ_E depends only on the ℚ-isomorphism class of E; it is finite by the finiteness of the prime degrees of rational isogenies (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.6) and because only finitely many ℓ have v_ℓ(N) = 1, each with v_ℓ(j_E) a fixed negative integer.
proofSteps: Rational cyclic p-subgroups C give ℚ-isogenies E → E/C of degree p; there are finitely many E/C up to ℚ-isomorphism (finiteness of the isogeny class), and for each E′ the nonzero Hom_ℚ(E, E′) = ℤ·f₀ has degrees d·n², so only finitely many primes p occur as degrees (R28.6: End_ℚ(E) = ℤ, rank-one Hom).
The multiplicative-reduction condition is finite: finitely many ℓ ∥ N, each with v_ℓ(j_E) ≠ 0.
Assemble the four finite sets.
acceptance: Keep Σ_E as data: every later step says which of its clauses it uses.
Do not assume Serre's open-image theorem or exclude CM curves: the finiteness argument uses only R28.6.
Mazur's bound (p > 163 for irreducibility) is a sharper, unread input; it is not needed for finiteness.

sources.locator: §4.6, p. 207 (printed page; Collège de France PDF page 29)

nodes.title: The residual conductor divides N
nodes.statement: For every prime p, the prime-to-p Artin conductor N(ρ̄_{E,p}) of E[p] divides N; at each ℓ ≠ p the exponent of ℓ in N(ρ̄_{E,p}) is at most v_ℓ(N).
hypotheses: Conductors: the Artin conductor of the residual representation away from p and the conductor of E through its ℓ-adic Tate modules (R01.6's conductor interface).
proofSteps: At ℓ ≠ p, the tame part dim E[p] − dim E[p]^{I_ℓ} ≤ 2 − dim V_r(E)^{I_ℓ} for r ≠ ℓ, since invariants of the reduction contain the reduction of the invariants; the wild (Swan) part is the same for E[p] and V_r(E), because wild inertia is a pro-ℓ group acting through a finite quotient of order prime to p.
acceptance: Serre notes that divisibility alone suffices for Theoreme 4.

sources.locator: §4.6, p. 207 (printed page; Collège de France PDF page 29)
sources.match: Divisibility, with Serre's remark that it suffices.

nodes.title: When the residual conductor equals N
nodes.statement: For p ≥ 5: N(ρ̄_{E,p}) = N iff (a) p ∤ N and (b) p ∤ v_ℓ(j_E) for every ℓ with v_ℓ(N) = 1. In particular N(ρ̄_{E,p}) = N for every p ∉ Σ_E.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 is what makes the additive places harmless: the image of inertia at an additive place of potentially good reduction has order dividing 24.
proofSteps: If p ∣ N then p divides N but not the prime-to-p conductor: (a) is necessary.
At ℓ ∥ N (multiplicative reduction) E is, up to an unramified quadratic twist, the Tate curve with parameter q, v_ℓ(q) = −v_ℓ(j_E); E[p] is unramified at ℓ iff p ∣ v_ℓ(q). This is condition (b).

At additive ℓ, V_r(E)^{I_ℓ} = 0 and the inertia image is finite of order dividing 24 (potentially good) or acts through a nontrivial quadratic character times a unipotent (potentially multiplicative); for p ≥ 5 the reduction E[p]^{I_ℓ} is also 0 and the Swan conductors agree, so the exponents are equal.
acceptance: Test: a semistable E with ℓ ∥ N and p ∣ v_ℓ(j_E) has N(ρ̄_{E,p}) = N/ℓ (the level-lowering situation).
Serre gives the criterion with 'on vérifie' and no proof; the argument here follows the Tate curve at ℓ.

sources.locator: §4.6, p. 207 (printed page; Collège de France PDF page 29)

nodes.title: Lemme 5: E[p] is absolutely irreducible with conductor N for p ∉ Σ_E
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ have conductor N. Then det ρ̄_{E,p} = χ̄_p (the mod-p cyclotomic character), and for every p ∉ Σ_E: (4.6.2) ρ̄_{E,p} is absolutely irreducible, and (4.6.3) its prime-to-p conductor is N.
hypotheses: Irreducibility over F_p is the rational-isogeny clause of Σ_E; absolute irreducibility for odd p follows from oddness (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4).
proofSteps: det ρ̄_{E,p} = χ̄_p by the Weil pairing (R01.6).
A Galois-stable line in E[p] is a ℚ-rational cyclic subgroup of order p, excluded for p ∉ Σ_E.
Odd p with det = χ̄ odd: irreducible over F_p implies absolutely irreducible (R01.4).
Conductor: residual-conductor-equality.
acceptance: The CM case is included: nothing uses a large image.

sources.locator: §4.6, p. 207 (printed page; Collège de France PDF page 29)

sources.match: The oddness argument, owned by R01.4.

nodes.title: Weight two and trivial character at good primes
nodes.statement: For p ∉ Σ_E (so E has good reduction at p and p ≥ 7), E[p] extends to a finite flat group scheme over ℤ_p (the p-torsion of the Néron model), so ρ̄_{E,p} is finite at p; with det ρ̄_{E,p} = χ̄_p, Serre's recipe gives weight k(ρ̄_{E,p}) = 2 and character ε = 1.
hypotheses: p odd: Serre's Proposition 4 (k = 2 iff det|_I = χ and finite at p) is proved for p ≠ 2; excluding p ≤ 5 avoids the boundary.
proofSteps: Good reduction: the Néron model is an abelian scheme over ℤ_p and its p-torsion is finite flat (R07.6).
Serre §1.3: ε is read off from det ρ̄ = χ̄^{k−1}ε, so det = χ̄ forces ε = 1 once k = 2.
Serre's Proposition 4 (R15.4's recipe): det|_{I_p} = χ̄ and finiteness at p give k = 2.
acceptance: Record that the character is trivial directly from det = χ̄, not from a characteristic-zero nebentypus.

nodes.title: Serre witnesses at level N
nodes.statement: For each p ∉ Σ_E the classical Serre theorem (ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6) gives a normalised eigenform f_p ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N), F̄_p) — equivalently a normalised newform g_p of weight 2, level N(ρ̄) = N, trivial character, with a prime λ_p | p of its coefficient field — such that ρ̄_{g_p, λ_p} ≅ ρ̄_{E,p}. Its Hecke eigenvalues satisfy a_ℓ(g_p) ≡ a_ℓ(E) mod λ_p for every ℓ ∤ Np.
hypotheses: p ∉ Σ_E; the level is the prime-to-p conductor, equal to N by Lemme 5.
The witness is used only through its Hecke eigensystem mod λ_p; no claim is made that it has coefficients in F_p (Serre's (3.2.6?) rationality is not used).
proofSteps: Check the hypotheses of R27.6 for ρ̄_{E,p}: odd (det = χ̄), absolutely irreducible, conductor N, weight 2, character 1.
Apply R27.6 to obtain (g_p, λ_p) and the isomorphism of residual representations.
Traces at ℓ ∤ Np: a_ℓ(E) is the trace of Frob_ℓ on E[p] (R01.6) and a_ℓ(g_p) mod λ_p is the trace on ρ̄_{g_p}.
acceptance: Non-circularity: R27.6 must not rest on the modularity of E. SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6's elliptic export (weight-two newform at the reduced level) assumes E modular and is therefore not a prerequisite here.
The witness lives at level exactly N (not a divisor) because N(ρ̄_{E,p}) = N for p ∉ Σ_E.

sources.match: The weight-two case of Serre's conjecture (now R27.6).

sources.locator: §4.6, p. 207 (printed page; Collège de France PDF page 29)

nodes.title: Trivial nebentypus from its reduction
nodes.statement: Let ε be a Dirichlet character of modulus N with values in a number field K and λ | p a prime of K. If ε ≡ 1 mod λ and p ∤ φ(N), then ε = 1. (Needed only by a route that first produces a characteristic-zero newform of unknown nebentypus; the direct route of finite-flat-weight-two gets ε = 1 from det ρ̄ = χ̄.)
hypotheses: p ∤ φ(N): the values of ε are roots of unity of order dividing φ(N).
proofSteps: The values of ε are m-th roots of unity with m ∣ φ(N).
For p ∤ m, reduction modulo λ is injective on μ_m (X^m − 1 is separable mod p), so ε(a) ≡ 1 forces ε(a) = 1.
acceptance: Non-example when p ∣ φ(N): N = 5, p = 2; the quadratic character of conductor 5 is nontrivial but ≡ 1 mod any prime above 2.

sources.match: Serre's direct route; the φ(N) route is the alternative RS-06 asks to distinguish.

nodes.title: One form for infinitely many primes
nodes.statement: If P is an infinite set of primes and F : P → 𝓔 is any map to a finite set 𝓔, then some fibre F⁻¹(f) is infinite.
hypotheses: 𝓔 finite.
proofSteps: Mathlib's Finite.exists_infinite_fiber applied to the infinite type P.
acceptance: Applied with 𝓔 the finite set of normalised weight-two newforms of level dividing N.

nodes.title: An algebraic integer in infinitely many primes is zero
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and α ∈ 𝒪_K. If for infinitely many rational primes p there is a prime 𝔭 | p of 𝒪_K with α ∈ 𝔭, then α = 0.
hypotheses: The primes p are distinct; one prime above each suffices.
proofSteps: α ∈ 𝔭 implies p ∣ N_{K/ℚ}(α) ∈ ℤ.
A nonzero integer has finitely many prime divisors, so N(α) = 0, hence α = 0.
acceptance: Test: α = 2 lies in primes above only p = 2.

nodes.title: A single newform with the Frobenius traces of E
nodes.statement: There is a normalised newform F of weight 2, trivial character and level dividing N such that A_ℓ(F) = a_ℓ(E) for every prime ℓ ∤ N.
hypotheses: The witnesses g_p of R29.2 are newforms of level N; the set 𝓔_N of normalised newforms of weight 2 and level dividing N is finite (Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 4).
proofSteps: For p ∉ Σ_E take g_p ∈ 𝓔_N (lifting through Deligne–Serre where the witness is given only mod p).
Pigeonhole: some F ∈ 𝓔_N equals g_p for p in an infinite set P.
For ℓ ∤ N and p ∈ P ∖ {ℓ}: A_ℓ(F) − a_ℓ(E) ∈ λ_p, so A_ℓ(F) = a_ℓ(E) by algebraic-integer-norm-vanishing.
acceptance: Only the good coefficients are compared here; bad coefficients and exact level are R29.4.

sources.locator: §4.6, p. 207 (printed page; Collège de France PDF page 29)

nodes.title: The newform F_E attached to E
nodes.statement: F_E is the unique normalised newform of weight 2 and trivial character, of some level M_E | N, with A_ℓ(F_E) = a_ℓ(E) for all ℓ ∤ N. Uniqueness is strong multiplicity one; its Fourier coefficients are rational integers (rational-coefficient-field).
hypotheses: Uniqueness among newforms of all levels dividing N (Tau Ceti HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.eq_of_forall_notMem_eigenvalue_eq).
proofSteps: Existence: the theorem above.
Uniqueness: two newforms with the same eigenvalues outside N coincide (strong multiplicity one).
acceptance: The level M_E is shown to equal N in R29.4 (exact-conductor).

uses.how: its level is compared with the conductor of E.
A_{F_E} is the modular quotient attached to it.
the modular parametrisation and the newform of a modular elliptic curve.

nodes.title: F_E has rational integer coefficients
nodes.statement: The coefficient field of F_E is ℚ, and all its Fourier coefficients (including A_ℓ for ℓ | N) are rational integers.
hypotheses: Fixed level and trivial character; Galois conjugates of newforms are newforms (Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8g).
proofSteps: For σ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ), F_E^σ is a newform of the same level and character with A_ℓ(F_E^σ) = σ(a_ℓ(E)) = a_ℓ(E) for ℓ ∤ N.
Strong multiplicity one gives F_E^σ = F_E, so every coefficient is σ-fixed, hence rational; coefficients of newforms are algebraic integers, so they lie in ℤ.
acceptance: Serre only records that the good A_ℓ lie in ℤ; the bad coefficients are rational by this conjugation argument.

sources.match: The good coefficients; the rest follows by conjugation.

nodes.title: The Tate module of E is the Galois representation of F_E
nodes.statement: For every prime r, V_r(E) ≅ V_r(F_E) as ℚ_r[G_ℚ]-modules, where V_r(F_E) is the r-adic representation attached to F_E (Eichler–Shimura, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations).
hypotheses: V_r(E) is semisimple (Faltings, R28.6); V_r(F_E) is semisimple (irreducible, from the Eichler–Shimura construction).
proofSteps: For ℓ ∤ Nr both representations are unramified at ℓ with characteristic polynomial X² − a_ℓ X + ℓ (R01.6 for E, Eichler–Shimura for F_E).
Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt (R01.5) identify the semisimplifications; both are semisimple, hence isomorphic.
acceptance: Characteristic polynomials, not traces alone, when comparing residually.

nodes.title: The level of F_E is the conductor of E
nodes.statement: The level M_E of F_E equals the conductor N of E.
hypotheses: Local–global compatibility at every finite place, including monodromy (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.4), and the conductor of E defined through V_r(E) (Ogg's formula).
proofSteps: The conductor of V_r(F_E) (as a Weil–Deligne representation at each ℓ ≠ r) equals the level M_E (Carayol, R19.4).
The conductor of V_r(E) equals N (Ogg–Saito, through R01.6's conductor interface).
The two representations are isomorphic (tate-module-comparison), so M_E = N.
acceptance: Equality of unramified traces alone does not give the conductor; the full local comparison is used.

sources.match: Carayol's corollary: for a rational newform the conductor equals the level.

nodes.title: All local factors agree
nodes.statement: For every prime ℓ, the local factor of E (Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.localPolynomial: 1 − a_ℓT + ℓT² at good ℓ, 1 ∓ T at split/nonsplit multiplicative ℓ, 1 at additive ℓ) equals the local factor 1 − A_ℓ(F_E)T + 𝟙_{ℓ∤N} ℓT² of F_E. Equivalently A_ℓ(F_E) = +1, −1, 0 according as E has split multiplicative, nonsplit multiplicative or additive reduction at ℓ | N.
hypotheses: Uses the Weil–Deligne comparison at ℓ | N, not only traces.
proofSteps: For ℓ ∤ N: A_ℓ = a_ℓ by R29.3.

For ℓ | N: the local factor of both sides is det(1 − Frob_ℓ T | V_r^{I_ℓ}); compute it for E by reduction type (Tate curve for multiplicative, zero invariants for additive) and for F_E by R19.4, then use the isomorphism V_r(E) ≅ V_r(F_E).
acceptance: Check the sign convention against Mathlib's localPolynomial (split multiplicative gives 1 − T).

sources.match: Equality of L-functions, hence of every local factor.

nodes.title: E is isogenous to the modular quotient A_{F_E}
nodes.statement: The modular quotient A_{F_E} of J₀(N) (ModularCurvesPartII R14.5) is an elliptic curve over ℚ, and there is a ℚ-isogeny A_{F_E} → E.
hypotheses: dim A_{F_E} = [K_{F_E} : ℚ] = 1 by rational-coefficient-field.
proofSteps: A_{F_E} is an elliptic curve with V_r(A_{F_E}) ≅ V_r(F_E) (R14.5 with the Tate-module identification of R19.6).
V_r(A_{F_E}) ≅ V_r(E) by tate-module-comparison; Faltings' isogeny criterion gives a ℚ-isogeny.
acceptance: The isogeny is over ℚ: Faltings' criterion is applied over the base field ℚ.

nodes.title: The modular parametrisation X₀(N) → E
nodes.statement: φ_E : X₀(N) → E is the composite of the Abel–Jacobi map X₀(N) → J₀(N) normalised at the rational cusp ∞, the quotient J₀(N) → A_{F_E} and a ℚ-isogeny A_{F_E} → E. It is a nonconstant morphism of curves over ℚ with φ_E(∞) = O, and φ_E^*ω_E = c · 2πi F_E(z)dz for a nonzero constant c (Manin's constant).
hypotheses: The Abel–Jacobi map and its universal property: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer F; the rational cusp: ModularCurvesPartII R14.6.
proofSteps: The Abel–Jacobi image of X₀(N) generates J₀(N), and J₀(N) → A_{F_E} → E is surjective, so φ_E is nonconstant.
The pullback of the invariant differential lies in the F_E-eigenspace of holomorphic differentials.
acceptance: The map is a morphism over ℚ, not a divisor class; its degree is positive.
Over ℂ, φ_E is z ↦ 2πi∫_{i∞}^z F_E(w)dw mod Λ, followed by the isogeny (Cremona §2.15.1).

nodes.title: Modularity of elliptic curves over ℚ
nodes.statement: Every elliptic curve E/ℚ of conductor N is modular: equivalently (i) there is a normalised newform F ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) with rational integer coefficients and A_p(F) = a_p(E) for all primes p (with the bad-prime convention of bad-euler-factors); (ii) E is ℚ-isogenous to a quotient of J₀(N); (iii) there is a nonconstant morphism X₀(N) → E over ℚ. The proof is unconditional through the classical Serre theorem (ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6).
hypotheses: Scope: elliptic curves over ℚ only.
proofSteps: (i) is newform-of-E with exact-conductor and bad-euler-factors; (ii) is isogeny-to-E; (iii) is modular-parametrisation.

Conversely (iii) ⇒ (i): pulling back ω_E gives a nonzero weight-two cusp form of level N, an eigenform by the Hecke compatibility of the Jacobian quotient (Eichler–Shimura), whose newform has the traces of E.
acceptance: Dependency check: the chain R29.1–R29.5 uses R27.6 but no statement that assumes E modular.

nodes.title: What Théorème 4 asserts and its scope
nodes.statement: Serre's Théorème 4 derives the Taniyama–Weil conjecture for E/ℚ from the case ε = 1, k = 2 of his conjecture. The companion Théorème 5 (abelian varieties over ℚ with real multiplication by a totally real field of degree dim X are quotients of J₀(N), N the dim-th root of the conductor) is recorded as a separately scoped inherited target; no general GL₂-type modularity, rank formula or Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer statement is asserted.
hypotheses: Théorème 5 needs K_X totally real of degree exactly n = dim X.
proofSteps: Record the implication chain of R29.1–R29.5 and its unconditional input R27.6.
State Théorème 5's hypotheses and leave its proof to a future owner.

gaps.title: Mazur's rational-isogeny theorem is an unread import
gaps.detail: Verified: Serre's Lemme 5 and its attribution 'd'apres Mazur [29], (4.6.2) est vrai des que p > 163'. Not verified: Mazur's theorem. Searched the supplied library: CATALOGUE.json contains no record for Mazur, 'Rational isogenies of prime degree', Invent. Math. 44 (1978); the Mazur items present are ADD_MAZUR89 (Deforming Galois representations), ADD_MazurWiles_AbelianExtensions (Class fields of abelian extensions of Q) and ADD_MazurSwinnertonDyer_WeilCurves (Arithmetic of Weil curves). Note that Serre observes the argument only needs N_p to DIVIDE N, so the sharp constant 163 is not essential to Theoreme 4; but irreducibility of rho_p for all but finitely many p is. Next source action: obtain Mazur, Invent. Math. 44 (1978), 129-162, and read the theorem on rational points of X_0(p); alternatively record the weaker statement that E[p] is irreducible for all but finitely many p, which follows from Faltings finiteness as the stage text itself proposes. Checkpoint cc-39fac3 (2026-09-28): the argument no longer needs Mazur's theorem; finiteness of the exceptional primes comes from R28.6 (finite prime degrees of rational isogenies). The sharp bound p > 163 remains an unread refinement.
